title: Boss: the release manager
summary: Compute versions from commits, find the latest release and drive a canary rollout to the end.

steps.title: Release day
steps.body: You are automating the release manager's job: pick the version, find what is currently released, and run a progressive rollout with flags and canaries.

steps.title: Version from Conventional Commits
prompt: Commit messages follow **Conventional Commits**: `type(scope)!: description`. Write `string NextVersion(string current, List<string> commits)`:
- the part before the first `:` ends with `!`, or the message contains `BREAKING CHANGE` → major
Apply only the **largest** bump once. No bump at all returns `current`. Versions are plain `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.
hints: Track the biggest bump seen as a number: 0 none, 1 patch, 2 minor, 3 major.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("fixes only", "1.4.3", NextVersion("1.4.2", new() { "fix: rounding", "fix(api): null check" }));
Dojo.Eq("a feature wins over fixes", "1.5.0", NextVersion("1.4.2", new() { "fix: a", "feat(orders): history endpoint", "docs: readme" }));
Dojo.Eq("bang means breaking", "2.0.0", NextVersion("1.4.2", new() { "feat(api)!: remove v1 routes" }));
Dojo.Eq("BREAKING CHANGE footer", "2.0.0", NextVersion("1.4.2", new() { "refactor: ids\n\nBREAKING CHANGE: ids are now strings" }));
Dojo.Eq("nothing to release", "1.4.2", NextVersion("1.4.2", new() { "chore: bump tooling", "test: more cases" }));

steps.title: Latest stable release
prompt: Write `string? LatestRelease(List<string> tags)`. Tags look like `v1.4.2`. Consider only tags that match exactly `v` + `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`
(no pre-releases, no other tags) and return the highest **by numeric comparison**, including the `v`. Return `null` if there is none.
hints: Order by each number descending; `FirstOrDefault` returns null on an empty sequence.
template: using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
{{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("numeric, not text", "v1.10.0", LatestRelease(new() { "v1.2.0", "v1.10.0", "v1.9.3" }));
Dojo.Eq("pre-releases ignored", "v2.0.0", LatestRelease(new() { "v2.0.0", "v2.1.0-rc.1", "nightly", "v1.99.0" }));
Dojo.Check("no releases yet", LatestRelease(new() { "nightly", "v0.1" }) == null, "expected null");

steps.title: Feature flag evaluation
prompt: Write `bool IsEnabled(bool killSwitch, List<string> allowList, int percent, string userId)`:
1. if `killSwitch` is true the feature is off for everyone
3. otherwise use the same FNV-1a bucket as `Route` (`h % 100 < percent`)
starter: bool IsEnabled(bool killSwitch, List<string> allowList, int percent, string userId)
solution: bool IsEnabled(bool killSwitch, List<string> allowList, int percent, string userId)
foreach (byte b in Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(userId)) { h ^= b; h *= 16777619; }
hints: The order of the rules matters: the kill switch beats the allow list.
Copy the hashing loop from the canary splitter.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("kill switch beats the allow list", false, IsEnabled(true, new() { "staff1" }, 100, "staff1"));
Dojo.Eq("allow list at 0%", true, IsEnabled(false, new() { "staff1" }, 0, "staff1"));
Dojo.Eq("0% for normal users", false, IsEnabled(false, new(), 0, "alice"));
Dojo.Eq("100% for normal users", true, IsEnabled(false, new(), 100, "alice"));
Dojo.Eq("bucket of \"a\" is 20: off at 20%", false, IsEnabled(false, new(), 20, "a"));
Dojo.Eq("bucket of \"a\" is 20: on at 21%", true, IsEnabled(false, new(), 21, "a"));

steps.title: Drive the rollout
prompt: Write `string Rollout(List<int> steps, List<double> canaryErrorPct, double stableErrorPct)`. `steps` are the canary percentages in order
(e.g. `1, 5, 25, 100`) and `canaryErrorPct[i]` is what was measured at step `i`.
Walk the steps; at the first step where the canary is more than **1.0** point worse than stable, return `"rolled back at 25%"`
(with that step's percent). If every step is healthy return `"promoted to 100%"` (with the last step's percent).
starter: string Rollout(List<int> steps, List<double> canaryErrorPct, double stableErrorPct)
solution: string Rollout(List<int> steps, List<double> canaryErrorPct, double stableErrorPct)
hints: A `for` loop gives you the index for both lists.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("healthy all the way", "promoted to 100%", Rollout(new() { 1, 5, 25, 100 }, new() { 0.5, 0.4, 0.6, 0.5 }, 0.5));
Dojo.Eq("fails at 25%", "rolled back at 25%", Rollout(new() { 1, 5, 25, 100 }, new() { 0.5, 0.9, 3.0, 0.5 }, 0.5));
Dojo.Eq("fails immediately", "rolled back at 1%", Rollout(new() { 1, 50 }, new() { 9.0, 0.0 }, 0.2));
Dojo.Eq("stops at the plan's last step", "promoted to 50%", Rollout(new() { 10, 50 }, new() { 0.1, 0.1 }, 0.1));
